quotes.text: Shadow data isn't hidden because someone is malicious. It's hidden because your governance model was never designed for visibility first.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes shadow data as an architectural rather than a behavioral problem.

quotes.text: Shadow data is any unknown, hidden or overlooked copy of sensitive information that exists outside your IT security and governance frameworks. It's not the same as shadow IT.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A precise definition that separates shadow data from shadow IT.

quotes.text: Your governance policy might be correct, but if your map of the environment lags reality by months, the policy is governing a fiction.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the latency-of-enforcement problem behind manual governance.

quotes.text: classification tells you what the data is, but lineage tells you where it came from and where it went and that's where shadow data becomes visible.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly states why lineage, not classification alone, reveals shadow data.

quotes.text: You have an architecture problem, not a people problem. The solution is to streamline the request process not to punish the team for finding a workaround.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts the response to shadow data from blame to fixing slow official processes.

takeaways: Shadow data is the unknown copies of sensitive information outside your governance frameworks, and periodic manual audits cannot keep up with how fast it is created.
Microsoft Purview works discover-first: automated scans, custom classifiers and lineage reveal where sensitive data lives, how it moves and who created each copy.
Discovery only pays off when it is operationalized with labels, retention, stewards and shift-left remediation, which also makes your data estate ready for AI and regulations like the EU AI Act.
hook: Your data map only shows the data someone remembered to register, while forgotten storage accounts, OneDrive copies and AI training sets keep spreading sensitive information. This episode is for data governance, security and compliance teams who want to use Microsoft Purview to discover, classify and trace shadow data before it turns into a breach or a failed audit.
